title: Triangle Trade Adventure
welcome_lead: Set sail with British merchants across three continents in the Transatlantic Slave Trade. ⚓
meta_desc: Triangle Trade Adventure — a KS3 walkthrough of the three legs of the transatlantic slave trade.
final_note: You mapped the three legs of the triangle trade and saw why merchants made huge profits.

concepts.def: Trader who buys and sells goods
Items made in factories like guns, cloth

walkthroughs.body_html:
British ships set off from ports like Bristol, Liverpool and London.

They carried manufactured goods — guns, gunpowder, cloth, iron bars, beads and brandy.

On the West African coast (in modern Ghana, Nigeria and Senegal), captains traded these goods with African rulers and slave dealers for captured Africans. 🏴

This was the Middle Passage, the horrific journey across the Atlantic.

Captives were packed below deck in tiny spaces, chained together. The voyage took 6 to 12 weeks. Disease, suicide and brutal punishment killed many.

Survivors were sold at slave markets in the Caribbean, Brazil and the American colonies.

The ships now headed home — but not empty.

They carried raw materials grown by enslaved people: sugar, tobacco, cotton, coffee and rum.

Back in Britain these were sold for huge profits. Some money paid for new manufactured goods, ready for the triangle to begin again. 💷

mcqs.q: Why did William the Conqueror commission the Domesday Book in 1086?
options: The 1928 Act gave women in Britain the vote for the first time.
To record landholding and resources so he could assess taxation (geld), confirm Norman tenants' rights, and settle disputes over confiscated Anglo-Saxon estates.
It was a census of the English population, like a modern one.
It was a list of Anglo-Saxon rebels William wanted to execute.

mcqs.q: What did the 1928 Equal Franchise Act do?
options: It was a list of Anglo-Saxon rebels William wanted to execute.
It gave women the vote on the same terms as men — all adults over 21 — completing the process begun in 1918, which had only enfranchised women over 30 with property.
The 1918 Representation of the People Act gave all women the vote.
The 1928 Act gave women in Britain the vote for the first time.
